title: A datastore blocks in its socket while idle; its callers converge on it

problem.summary: Several services slow down and their slow call paths all end at the same downstream component. That component is not busy and is not short of CPU - it is blocked inside a single socket-waiting syscall for far longer than usual. Because it emits no request traces of its own, the call graph can only point at its nearest traced caller, so the traces accuse a victim and only the kernel identifies the real culprit.
symptoms: caller latency inflates sharply, often by orders of magnitude
the slow call edges all converge on one shared downstream component
that component is resource-quiet: CPU flat or falling, no disk or memory pressure
requests still succeed, so error rates barely move

discriminators.signal: blocking-syscall duration of the suspect component
discriminators.this_problem: ONE socket-waiting syscall inflates by an order of magnitude while everything else stays flat
discriminators.not_this_problem: no syscall inflates by more than about 2x
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED from raw L0 via babeltrace2: the datastore poll p95 went 15.96 -> 587.70 ms = 36.83x (n=17,245). CONTROL, co-tenant run: the SAME syscall on the SAME component went 16.64 -> 18.72 ms = 1.12x (n=45,337). See evidence/L0_blocking_syscall_slowdb.json and evidence/L0_blocking_syscall_CONTROL_cotenant.json

discriminators.this_problem: flat - the component is not waiting for a CPU, it is waiting for a reply
discriminators.not_this_problem: runqueue delay inflates several-fold across many processes
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED: on the slow-datastore run the datastore runqueue delay was 1.09x and the median across 38 high-volume processes was 0.84x, i.e. unchanged. On the co-tenant run the busiest application process was 7.12x. See evidence/L0_runqueue_delay_slowdb.json

discriminators.this_problem: slow edges converge on ONE component that has no slow outgoing edges of its own
discriminators.not_this_problem: nothing converges; edge slowdowns stay near 1x
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED: convergence on a single component at 717.7x incoming with zero slow outgoing edges. CONTROL, co-tenant run: converged_on = null, max 1.7x. See evidence/L0_edge_convergence_slowdb.json

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the converged-on component shows dominant off-CPU external I/O wait, and that is what identifies it
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: off_cpu_io_wait is 98-99% for EVERY fault family measured (slow_db 99.4, dependency_outage 98.2, svc_cpu_cap 98.0). The coarse buckets are dominated by idle waiting, so they cannot separate anything. See evidence/wait_signature_all_families.json
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: replaced by the family_seconds split, which is where any real signal lives.
unverified_do_not_claim.agent_note: A dominant off-CPU external-I/O SHARE on the suspect. Measured at 98-99% for every labelled fault, because that share is dominated by ordinary idle waiting. Use the DURATION of the specific blocking syscall instead.

known_limitation.what: the call graph names a VICTIM, not the culprit
known_limitation.detail: The injected fault was on the datastore, but convergence lands on its caller because the datastore emits no request spans. Traces get you one hop away; only the kernel evidence identifies the component that is actually blocked.
known_limitation.evidence: MEASURED: ground truth target was the datastore, convergence returned its caller at 717.7x. See evidence/L0_edge_convergence_slowdb.json

reproduction.system: Sock Shop or Train Ticket on Ubuntu 24.04, LTTng 2.15, Docker 27+, single GCP n2 VM. Toxiproxy sits permanently in the datastore path so latency can be toggled without restarting anything.

logs: error-rate change per container, to confirm calls succeed rather than fail
traces: caller to callee edge latency, baseline versus incident, so convergence can be seen
collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. The verdict rests on how long the component blocks inside its socket-waiting syscall, so entry AND exit of those calls are required - entry alone gives no duration. The two scheduler events are needed for the negative control: showing runqueue delay is FLAT is what rules out CPU starvation. This is strictly more than the CPU-contention blueprint needs, and that difference is the point: the two problems genuinely require different collection orders.

processing.step: Stage the raw kernel trace (channels are stored gzipped)
processing.expect: CTF 2 metadata plus channel0_* streams; needs babeltrace 2.1 or newer

processing.step: Find which component the slow call paths converge on
processing.expect: one component with slow incoming and no slow outgoing edges. Remember it may be the CALLER of the culprit if the culprit emits no spans

processing.step: Measure how long the suspect and its neighbours block inside each syscall
processing.expect: one socket-waiting syscall inflated by roughly an order of magnitude; everything else near 1x

processing.step: NEGATIVE CONTROL: confirm the suspect is not merely CPU-starved
processing.expect: runqueue delay flat, about 1x. If it inflates broadly, this is the CPU-contention blueprint instead

processing.step: Combine into the verdict and its artifacts
processing.expect: a named component, the syscall it blocked in, its inflation factor, and the flat runqueue delay that rules out CPU starvation

outputs.contains: the blocked component, the syscall and its inflation, the convergence point, and the runqueue-delay control
syscall duration p95 baseline vs incident, per component and syscall
what was waiting, on what, and why its callers are victims

verdict_when: one component socket-waiting syscall inflates by roughly an order of magnitude
that component runqueue delay stays flat, so it is not short of CPU
slow call edges converge on it or on its nearest traced caller
traffic continues to succeed, so error rates barely move

rule_out.when: runqueue delay inflates broadly across many processes while no syscall inflates much
calls fail or hang to timeout instead of returning slowly
the inflated wait is a disk syscall and other disk users degrade too

decision.root_cause_is: the converged-on datastore component itself, never its callers, which are victims

evidence_from_literature.claim: Blocking-syscall attribution distinguishes a component that is slow from a component that is waiting, which utilisation metrics cannot do
evidence_from_literature.validated_on: our labelled slow-datastore runs; on Sock Shop this verdict survives even with traces removed entirely

provenance.notes: v3: rebuilt on the raw kernel trace. The decisive measurement is a single syscall duration - 36.83x here versus 1.12x for the same syscall on the same component under the CPU fault. Also records the honest limitation that the call graph names the victim, because the culprit emits no spans.
